page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. Powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, this instance features 128 dedicated virtual CPUs. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration caters specifically to parallelized execution patterns that require substantial processing capacity per memory unit.

The hardware profile lacks integrated local storage, meaning data persistence relies on external network-attached block storage. Hardware acceleration is absent, as the system includes zero GPUs. Network capabilities are a key specification of this instance, offering a baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps to handle high-volume inter-node data transfers.

With its dedicated CPU allocation paired with high network throughput, the ecs.c7.32xlarge delivers significant core density for multi-threaded applications. The requirement for external storage represents a structural tradeoff for disk-bound tasks. The instance is suited for compute-intensive tasks such as continuous integration build arrays, batch processing pipelines, high-traffic web serving tiers, and distributed application microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.32xlarge is a high-density compute-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor. Driven by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 128 dedicated virtual CPUs combined with 256.0 GB of system memory. This yields a focused compute-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU, engineered for compute-heavy parallel applications. The configuration features no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent operational data, and omits hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is designed for demanding data communication with a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The ecs.c7.32xlarge provides high CPU core density relative to memory capacity, making it a resource-efficient choice for multi-threaded computing pipelines without requiring dedicated GPU acceleration. Appropriate workloads include continuous integration software build systems, batch processing platforms, compute-intensive web server arrays, and distributed enterprise application nodes.
